questions.stem: A pathology resident reviews an H&E-stained section and notices a cell whose cytoplasm is packed with ribosomes; the cytoplasm stains deep blue-purple rather than pink. Which of the following best explains this staining pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eosin binding to basic structures (eosinophilia)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematoxylin binding to acidic structures (basophilia)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Periodic acid reacting with carbohydrate-rich molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Silver impregnation of fine reticulin fiber networks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichrome dye binding to the cell's collagen fibers

explanation.summary: Hematoxylin stains acidic (basophilic) structures such as nuclei and ribosomes blue-purple.
explanation.whyCorrect: In H&E, hematoxylin binds acidic structures, which are therefore called basophilic; nuclei and ribosomes are the classic examples and stain blue-purple. Eosin binds basic (eosinophilic) structures such as cytoplasm and many extracellular proteins, staining them pink-red. A ribosome-rich cytoplasm therefore appears blue-purple.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eosin stains basic structures such as most cytoplasm and extracellular proteins pink-red, not blue-purple.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PAS is a separate stain for carbohydrate-rich structures; it is not part of a routine H&E.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Silver stains are used to show type III (reticulin) fibers, which are invisible on H&E.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Masson's trichrome stains collagen blue, but it is not part of H&E and ribosomes are not collagen.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man undergoes an abdominal fat pad biopsy for suspected amyloidosis. Congo red staining shows salmon-pink extracellular deposits. Which additional finding, seen when the same slide is examined under polarized light, is the hallmark of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apple-green birefringence of the deposits

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blue-purple staining of the deposits' nuclei

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bright blue granular pigment in the deposits

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dark black outlining of fine fibers in the deposits

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deep blue staining of collagen in the deposits

explanation.summary: Congo red stains amyloid salmon-pink to orange-red, with apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congo red is a water-soluble diazo dye that stains amyloid deposits salmon-pink to orange-red. Under polarized light the deposits show characteristic apple-green birefringence, which is the hallmark of amyloidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blue-purple nuclei reflect hematoxylin binding acidic structures; amyloid deposits are extracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bright blue pigment is the Prussian blue result for iron, not a polarized-light finding with Congo red.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dark fine fibers are the silver-stain appearance of reticulin, unrelated to amyloid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blue collagen is the result of Masson's trichrome, not of Congo red under polarized light.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: All four basic tissue types are made of cells and extracellular matrix. Which tissue type differs from the other three in that its extracellular matrix is abundant and carries out the tissue's main functions, while its cells are sparse and largely supportive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cardiac muscle tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Connective tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epithelial tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nervous tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skeletal muscle tissue

explanation.summary: Connective tissue is the tissue in which abundant ECM (fibers + ground substance) performs the main functions.
explanation.whyCorrect: In epithelial, muscle and nervous tissue, cells form the bulk of the tissue and carry out its unique functions, while the extracellular matrix is sparse and supportive. Connective tissue is the exception: its ECM of fibers and ground substance is abundant and does the main work, and its cells are typically sparse and supportive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardiac muscle, like other muscle, is dominated by its contractile cells rather than by matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: In epithelium, cells make up the bulk of the tissue and carry out its functions; the matrix is sparse.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nervous tissue function is carried out by its cells (neurons supported by glial cells), not by matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: In muscle, contractile cells form the bulk and perform the tissue's function.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has a deep forearm laceration repaired. A biopsy of the healing wound edge two weeks later shows plump spindle-shaped cells depositing new collagen, several of which are in mitosis. Which statement best describes these cells in normal, uninjured connective tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pluripotent cells that mainly regulate capillary blood flow

choices.label: B
choices.text: Resident cells that divide continuously to renew matrix

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resident cells that normally do not divide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resident cells that store, synthesize and release lipid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient cells that migrate in from the circulation

explanation.summary: Fibroblasts are resident connective tissue cells that divide only when wound healing is required.
explanation.whyCorrect: The collagen-producing cells of a healing wound are fibroblasts, which make collagen, elastic fibers and much of the ground substance. They are resident cells (originating within connective tissue) and do not normally undergo mitosis; the only time they divide is when wound healing is required.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes pericytes, which resemble fibroblasts but may modify capillary flow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibroblasts do not normally undergo mitosis; division is reserved for wound healing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This describes adipocytes, not the collagen-producing cells of a healing wound.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibroblasts are resident cells; they originate within connective tissue and stay there.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 24-year-old sprinter feels a pop at the back of his ankle and is found to have ruptured his Achilles tendon. Which collagen type predominates in the injured structure, and what is that collagen's key mechanical function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Type I collagen, resisting tension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Type II collagen, resisting pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type II collagen, resisting tension

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type III collagen, forming web-like stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type IV collagen, anchoring epithelial cells

explanation.summary: Tendons are dense regular connective tissue built of type I collagen, whose key function is resisting tension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type I collagen is the most common subtype, making up about 90% of the body's collagen. It is found in bone, skin, tendons, ligaments and organ capsules, and its key function is to resist tension. The tendon is the classic example of dense regular connective tissue made of parallel type I bundles.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Type II resists pressure but is found in hyaline cartilage, the vitreous body and nucleus pulposus, not tendon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tendon is not type II, and type II's role is resisting pressure rather than tension.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type III (reticulin) forms delicate networks in hematopoietic organs and around smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type IV is in the basal lamina of basement membranes and the lens capsule.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man undergoes surgery for a herniated lumbar disc, and the extruded gelatinous nucleus pulposus is sent to pathology. The predominant collagen in this material is the same type found in the vitreous body of the eye. What is the primary mechanical role of this collagen type?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allowing stretch and recoil of the tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anchoring epithelium to underlying tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forming a web-like stroma for marrow cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resisting pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resisting tension along one axis

explanation.summary: Type II collagen (hyaline cartilage, nucleus pulposus, vitreous body) primarily resists pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The nucleus pulposus and vitreous body both contain type II collagen, which is found primarily in hyaline cartilage matrix. The primary function of type II collagen fibers is to resist pressure, in contrast to type I collagen, which resists tension.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stretch and recoil are properties of elastic fibers, due to elastin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anchoring epithelium and aiding filtration are roles of type IV collagen in the basal lamina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Web-like stroma in bone marrow, spleen and lymph nodes is formed by type III (reticulin) collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Resisting tension is the key function of type I collagen, as in tendons and ligaments.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with thin, translucent, easily bruised skin and recurrent joint dislocations from hyperflexible joints presents with sudden severe abdominal pain; imaging shows a spontaneous perforation of the sigmoid colon. Her mother died of a ruptured aorta at age 38. A genetic defect in which fibers best explains her risk of bowel and large-artery rupture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elastic fibers cross-linked by desmosine in artery walls

choices.label: B
choices.text: Type I collagen fibers of bone, tendon and ligament

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type II collagen fibers of the hyaline cartilage matrix

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type III collagen fibers surrounding smooth muscle cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type IV collagen meshwork of the epithelial basal lamina

explanation.summary: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome results from defective type III collagen, which surrounds smooth muscle of the bowel and large arteries.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vascular EDS is caused by a genetic defect in transcribing or translating the DNA or mRNA that encodes type III collagen. Patients have thin, easily bruised, fragile skin and hyperflexible joints that may dislocate. Because type III fibers surround the smooth muscle cells of the bowel and large arteries, these patients are at risk of bowel and arterial rupture, so early diagnosis matters.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Elastic fibers allow stretch and recoil; the lecture ties vascular EDS to type III collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type I resists tension in bone and tendon; it is not the fiber surrounding smooth muscle in bowel and artery walls.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type II is found in cartilage, vitreous and nucleus pulposus and would not explain vessel or bowel rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type IV anchors epithelium in basement membranes; it is not the defect in vascular EDS.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A research group identifies an inherited defect in the collagen that forms the capsule of the lens of the eye. The same collagen type would also be expected to be abnormal in which of the following locations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Basal lamina of epithelial basement membranes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dentin and cementum of the permanent teeth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral discs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Parallel bundles of tendons and ligaments

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reticular stroma of lymph nodes and spleen

explanation.summary: Type IV collagen is found in the lens capsule and the basal lamina of basement membranes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type IV collagen forms a meshwork of fibers in the basal lamina of basement membranes and is also found in the lens capsule. In basement membranes it supports and anchors epithelial cells, aids filtration and acts as a scaffold for cell migration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dentin and cementum contain type I collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The nucleus pulposus contains type II collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tendons and ligaments are made of type I collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymph node and splenic stroma are built of type III (reticulin) collagen.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A punch biopsy of skin shows a deep layer composed of densely packed bundles of type I collagen oriented in a seemingly random fashion, with relatively few fibroblasts and minimal ground substance. For which mechanical demand is this arrangement best suited?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Permitting stretch to 150% followed by recoil

choices.label: B
choices.text: Providing a framework for hematopoietic cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resisting compressive pressure on the tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resisting tension applied along a single axis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resisting tension applied from many directions

explanation.summary: Dense irregular connective tissue (skin, organ capsules) resists multidirectional tension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dense irregular connective tissue, like dense regular, is mostly densely packed type I collagen with few fibroblasts and little ground substance, but its bundles run in many directions. This irregular arrangement makes it good at resisting tension from all directions, so it is found in places exposed to multidirectional pulling forces, such as the skin and organ capsules.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stretch and recoil depend on elastic fibers, not on dense type I bundles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is the role of reticular connective tissue made of type III fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Resisting pressure is the role of type II collagen in cartilage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Single-direction tension is handled by dense regular tissue with parallel bundles, as in tendons.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: An endoscopic biopsy of the colon is taken, and the pathologist examines the lamina propria that supports the thin surface epithelium. Which histologic features would be expected in this supporting layer on H&E?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fine fibers, many cell types, abundant clear ground substance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interwoven type III net visible only with silver stain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smooth glassy matrix of type II fibers blended with GAGs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thick parallel type I bundles with few interspersed cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thick randomly oriented type I bundles with few cells

explanation.summary: The lamina propria is loose (areolar) connective tissue: fine fibers, many cells, abundant clear ground substance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loose (areolar) connective tissue forms the lamina propria that supports the thin epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts. It contains fine collagen and elastic fibers, numerous cells such as fibroblasts, plasma cells and macrophages, and abundant optically clear ground substance that gives it an appearance of many little empty spaces.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This is reticular connective tissue of the marrow, lymph nodes and spleen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes hyaline cartilage, a specialized connective tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is dense regular connective tissue, as in tendons and ligaments.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is dense irregular connective tissue, as in the skin and organ capsules.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A lymph node is excised from a 50-year-old woman. On H&E, sheets of small lymphocytes are well seen, but the delicate fiber framework that supports them cannot be identified. Which stain would best demonstrate this framework?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congo red stain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giemsa stain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prussian blue stain

choices.label: E
choices.text: Silver stain

explanation.summary: Reticular (type III) fibers are invisible on H&E but easily identified with silver stains.
explanation.whyCorrect: The supporting framework of lymph nodes, bone marrow and spleen is reticular connective tissue, made of type III collagen (reticulin) fibers in an interwoven net. These fibers are invisible on regular H&E sections but are easily identified with silver stains, which show them as fine, darkly staining fibers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congo red identifies amyloid deposits, not supporting fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Giemsa is used for marrow, plasma cells, mast cells and blood parasites, not reticulin fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram stain differentiates bacteria by their cell walls.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prussian blue highlights iron deposits.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman who plays tennis has months of posterior heel pain that has not improved with stretching, ice, and NSAIDs. Ultrasound shows Achilles tendinopathy with disorganized fibers and edema. She is referred to physical therapy for an eccentric calf-strengthening program and told to avoid jumping and sprinting for now. By which mechanism is this program expected to help?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Converting tendon collagen from type I to type III fibers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing ground substance to cushion the tendon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Promoting a random, multidirectional collagen orientation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reducing tendon load so its collagen fibers can realign

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replacing damaged tendon collagen with elastic fibers

explanation.summary: In tendinopathy, eccentric strengthening offloads the tendon so its type I collagen can realign into parallel bundles.
explanation.whyCorrect: A tendon is dense regular connective tissue whose type I collagen bundles should run parallel, without edema. In tendinopathy the fibers are disorganized, making the tendon less flexible and painful. Eccentric strengthening strengthens the calf muscle, reducing load on the tendon, reducing edema and allowing realignment of the collagen fibers; ballistic motion is avoided in the meantime.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Healthy tendon is type I collagen; the goal is realignment, not conversion to reticulin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tendon has little ground substance; therapy aims to reduce edema and realign fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tendon is dense regular tissue; its fibers should be parallel, not random.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tendon strength comes from parallel type I bundles, not elastic fibers.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Histology and Histology of Connective Tissue

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had several months of gradually worsening weakness that began in her thighs and has since progressed; she now has difficulty rising from a chair. She is diagnosed with polymyositis and started on a glucocorticoid. In this disease, the inflammatory attack is centered on which connective tissue layer of skeletal muscle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endomysium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epimysium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perimysium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perineurium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sarcolemma

explanation.summary: Polymyositis is an inflammatory muscle disease that attacks skeletal muscle at the endomysium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endomysium is the delicate connective tissue surrounding each individual muscle cell. Polymyositis attacks muscle specifically at the endomysium, producing gradual loss of muscle tissue and weakness that begins in the thighs and progresses; it may respond to glucocorticoids.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The epimysium is the dense outer layer around the whole muscle, not the target described in polymyositis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The perimysium surrounds fascicles; the lecture places the polymyositis attack at the endomysium around individual cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The perineurium is a connective tissue covering that bundles axons in peripheral nerve, not a muscle layer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The sarcolemma is the muscle cell membrane, not a connective tissue layer.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A researcher stimulates one cardiac contractile myocyte in a culture of connected cells. The electrical impulse spreads to neighboring myocytes and they contract together, even though no nerve fibers are present in the culture. Which component of the intercalated discs directly permits this spread?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dense bodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fascia adherens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gap junctions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spot desmosomes (maculae adherens)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tight junctions

explanation.summary: Gap junctions in intercalated discs let current pass between cardiac myocytes, allowing contraction without direct nerve input to each cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intercalated discs contain gap junctions, spot desmosomes, and fascia adherens. Gap junctions provide a passage between cells that conducts electrical signals (and some ions) from one myocyte to the next, so cardiac cells can transmit impulses among themselves without input from innervating nerves.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dense bodies anchor actin and myosin to the sarcolemma in smooth muscle; they are not part of intercalated discs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fascia adherens join groups of myocytes like a broad belt for mechanical binding, not electrical conduction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spot desmosomes bind cardiac cells firmly together with cadherin-family proteins; they do not pass current.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tight junctions are not among the three junction types the lecture lists in intercalated discs.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A section of urinary bladder wall from a 60-year-old man shows tightly packed, spindle-shaped cells with centrally located, elongated nuclei and no cross-striations. The actin and myosin filaments in these cells are anchored to the sarcolemma by which structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dense bodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fascia adherens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intercalated discs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myofibrils

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sarcomeres

explanation.summary: Smooth muscle has actin and myosin but no sarcomeres or myofibrils; the filaments are anchored to the sarcolemma by dense bodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: The described cells are smooth muscle (spindle-shaped, central nuclei, no striations), which lines distensible organs like the bladder. Even without sarcomeres, smooth muscle contains actin and myosin, and these contractile proteins are anchored to the sarcolemma by dense bodies.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fascia adherens are belt-like junctions of cardiac intercalated discs, not filament anchors in smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intercalated discs are found only in cardiac muscle; smooth muscle cells are linked by gap junctions instead.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Smooth muscle lacks myofibrils; that absence is why it is not striated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Smooth muscle has no sarcomeres; actin and myosin are present but not arranged in sarcomeres.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A tissue block is taken from the sinoatrial node of a donor heart. Which statement correctly describes the autorhythmic cells it contains?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are long multinucleated cells with nuclei under the sarcolemma

choices.label: B
choices.text: They generate the heart's force by actin-myosin sliding in sarcomeres

choices.label: C
choices.text: They lack all innervation, so the brain cannot alter the heart rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: They link to contractile myocytes by gap junctions but do not contract

choices.label: E
choices.text: They make up the large majority of all cardiac muscle cells in the heart

explanation.summary: Autorhythmic (pacemaker) cells of the SA and AV nodes set heart rate, are autonomically innervated, connect to contractile cells by gap junctions, and do not contract.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac muscle has autorhythmic and contractile cells. Autorhythmic cells, including the SA and AV nodes, act as pacemakers that set the heart rate and are innervated by autonomic neurons. Gap junctions connect them to the surrounding contractile cells, but the pacemaker cells themselves do not contract.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Multiple peripheral nuclei describe skeletal muscle cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Force generation by sliding filaments is the job of contractile cells; pacemaker cells do not themselves contract.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Autorhythmic cells are innervated by autonomic neurons, which is how the brain controls the heart.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Contractile cells, not autorhythmic cells, compose the vast majority of cardiac muscle cells.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A pathologist compares myelin in a biopsy of a peripheral (sural) nerve with myelin in the optic nerve at autopsy. Which feature is true of the cell that produced the myelin in the sural nerve?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It contains GFAP intermediate filaments that maintain its form

choices.label: B
choices.text: It extends processes that blanket several axons at once

choices.label: C
choices.text: It forms thin sheaths around sensory neuron cell bodies

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lines the central canal and moves fluid with its cilia

choices.label: E
choices.text: It myelinates only one segment of a single axon

explanation.summary: In the PNS, Schwann cells produce myelin, each covering one segment of one axon, unlike oligodendrocytes, which myelinate multiple CNS axons.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peripheral nerve myelin is made by Schwann cells, which derive from the neural crest and migrate alongside developing axons. Unlike oligodendrocytes, which can myelinate multiple axons, a Schwann cell myelinates only one segment of one axon.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GFAP maintains the structure of astrocytes, which do not produce myelin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Myelinating multiple axons with processes is characteristic of oligodendrocytes in the CNS, such as the optic nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That describes satellite cells, which surround cell bodies in ganglia and do not myelinate axons.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That describes ependymal cells of the CNS.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has painful blurred vision in her right eye. Over the next year she develops numbness and tingling in her legs, poor coordination, and fatigue, with periods of remission in between. MRI shows lesions in the brain and spinal cord. Loss of myelin made by which cell type best explains her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Astrocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Microglia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oligodendrocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Satellite cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Schwann cells

explanation.summary: Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune demyelination of the CNS, where myelin is produced by oligodendrocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiple sclerosis demyelinates neurons of the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves, all CNS. CNS myelin, a phospholipid-protein insulator that increases conduction speed, is made by oligodendrocytes. Without it, neurons communicate poorly, producing optic neuritis, incoordination, numbness and tingling, and fatigue, with relapses and remissions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Astrocytes provide support, transport metabolites, and help form the blood-brain barrier, but they do not make myelin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Microglia are CNS macrophages that scavenge debris; they do not produce myelin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Satellite cells surround neuron cell bodies in PNS ganglia and do not make myelin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Schwann cells myelinate PNS axons; the lesions here are in the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerve (CNS).

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: An H&E section of spinal cord shows a large neuron cell body with a single nucleus containing a prominent nucleolus. Its cytoplasm is filled with coarse, deep-purple granular material. This granular material is composed mainly of which organelle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Golgi apparatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lysosomes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rough endoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum

explanation.summary: Nissl substance, the deep-purple granular material in neuron cell bodies, is abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neuron cell bodies contain a single nucleus, often with a prominent nucleolus, and cytoplasm with abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum. This appears deep purple and granular and is called Nissl substance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture identifies Nissl substance as rough endoplasmic reticulum, not Golgi.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lysosomes are not the basis of the purple granular Nissl substance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The deep-purple granular Nissl substance is rough endoplasmic reticulum, not mitochondria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nissl substance is rough, not smooth, endoplasmic reticulum; its granularity reflects ribosomes.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: Two processes leave the cell body of a neuron in an H&E section. At the base of process 1, the cytoplasm looks like the rest of the cell body, with purple granules. At the base of process 2, the cytoplasm is pale and free of granules. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Process 1 conducts impulses onward to other neurons

choices.label: B
choices.text: Process 1 is the axon, which arises at the axon hillock

choices.label: C
choices.text: Process 2 is a dendrite that gathers incoming stimuli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Process 2 is a glial process that lacks Nissl substance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Process 2 is the axon, which arises at the axon hillock

explanation.summary: The axon hillock is pale because it lacks Nissl substance, whereas the base of a dendrite looks like the rest of the cell body.
explanation.whyCorrect: Axons and dendrites can look alike, so the lecture says to examine where each branches from the cell body. A dendrite's base resembles the cell body, but the axon's base (the axon hillock) is pale because it is devoid of Nissl substance. The axon conducts impulses to other neurons.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conducting impulses to other neurons is the axon's job; process 1 is a dendrite that receives stimuli.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The axon hillock is pale because it lacks Nissl substance; process 1 has Nissl-like cytoplasm at its base, so it is a dendrite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dendrites have bases that resemble the cell body; the pale, Nissl-free base marks an axon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both processes leave the neuron's own cell body; the pale base is the axon hillock, not a glial process.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A biopsy of a spinal (dorsal root) ganglion is examined. The sensory neurons whose cell bodies lie in this ganglion would be expected to have which arrangement of processes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No axon and many branched dendrites

choices.label: B
choices.text: One axon and one dendrite only

choices.label: C
choices.text: One process that splits into two axons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several axons and a single dendrite

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several dendrites and a single axon

explanation.summary: Sensory neurons of spinal and cranial ganglia are pseudounipolar: one process leaves the cell body and splits into two axons, one acting as a dendrite.
explanation.whyCorrect: By morphology, pseudounipolar neurons are sensory neurons in spinal and cranial ganglia. A single process emerges from the cell body and splits into two axons, one of which acts as a dendrite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture describes no neuron type lacking an axon; spinal ganglion neurons are pseudounipolar.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two separate processes (one axon, one dendrite) describe bipolar neurons of the retina, olfactory mucosa, and inner ear.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No neuron type in the lecture has this arrangement; multipolar neurons have several dendrites and one axon.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Several dendrites with one axon describe multipolar neurons such as motor neurons and CNS interneurons.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: At autopsy, a 74-year-old man who had a stroke years earlier has an old cerebral infarct walled off by dense fibers. A silver stain shows that the cells forming this wall have innumerable cytoplasmic processes that were barely visible on H&E. Which other function is performed by this cell type?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conducting action potentials to effector sites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forming thin sheaths around ganglion cell bodies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lining the ventricles to move fluid with cilia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Producing myelin for several CNS axons

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taking up potassium and neurotransmitters

explanation.summary: Astrocytes form glial scars around old infarcts and also take up potassium and neurotransmitters, move metabolites, modulate blood flow, and help form the blood-brain barrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: Star-shaped astrocytes have processes whose GFAP stains well with silver but are inconspicuous on H&E; they form the dense glial scar around an old infarct. Astrocytes also provide structural support, modulate blood flow, move metabolites between capillaries and neurons with their perivascular feet, take up potassium and neurotransmitters, and help form the blood-brain barrier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glial cells, including astrocytes, do not conduct electrical impulses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is the role of satellite cells in the PNS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lining ventricles and moving CSF with cilia is done by ependymal cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myelinating multiple CNS axons is the role of oligodendrocytes, not the cells that form glial scars.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A brain biopsy from a region of tissue injury shows small, irregularly shaped cells with condensed chromatin migrating toward and clustering around cell debris. When activated, these cells can also perform which function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conducting action potentials

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forming the glial scar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myelinating several axons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presenting antigen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Producing cerebrospinal fluid

explanation.summary: Microglia are the specialized macrophages of the CNS: they migrate, scavenge debris, infectious agents, and damaged tissue, and present antigen when activated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small, irregular cells with condensed chromatin that migrate to injured tissue are microglia, the macrophages of the CNS. They scavenge cell debris, infectious agents, and damaged tissue, and when activated they can also present antigen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glial cells do not conduct electrical impulses; neurons do.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The dense-fiber glial scar around an old infarct is formed by astrocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myelinating CNS axons is the role of oligodendrocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CSF production involves ependymal cells and the choroid plexus, not microglia.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A section through the wall of a lateral ventricle shows a single layer of columnar to cuboidal epithelial cells, some bearing cilia, lining the ventricular space. Which statement about these cells is accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Modified forms of them contribute to the choroid plexus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their GFAP-filled processes form glial scars

choices.label: C
choices.text: They also line fascicles of peripheral nerves

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are resident macrophages that scavenge debris

choices.label: E
choices.text: They myelinate axons running in nearby white matter

explanation.summary: Ependymal cells line the ventricles and central canal, use cilia to move CSF, and in modified form help make up the CSF-producing choroid plexus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ependymal cells are columnar or cuboidal epithelial cells lining the brain's ventricles and the central canal of the spinal cord; some have cilia that move cerebrospinal fluid. Modified ependymal cells help form the choroid plexus, the network of blood vessels in the ventricles that produces CSF.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GFAP and glial scars are features of astrocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ependymal cells line the brain ventricles and the spinal central canal, a CNS location; perineurium bundles peripheral axons.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Scavenging macrophages of the CNS are microglia, not the epithelial cells lining ventricles.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CNS myelin is produced by oligodendrocytes.

questions.topicName: Histology of Muscle and Nervous Tissue

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy has had recurrent pneumonia and chronic sinus infections since infancy. A chest radiograph shows the cardiac apex on the right side, and CT shows dilated bronchi. A nasal mucosal biopsy is sent for electron microscopy. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of laminin within the lamina lucida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of the lamina densa beneath the epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of villin cross-links in microvillus cores

choices.label: D
choices.text: Missing dynein arms on the ciliary axonemes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replacement of columnar cells by stratified squamous cells

explanation.summary: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener subtype: situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis) results from axonemes lacking the dynein motor protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: In primary ciliary dyskinesia the ciliary axonemes lack dynein, the motor protein that drives the ciliary beat, so ciliary movement is ineffective. Respiratory cilia cannot clear inhaled particulates, producing recurrent lower respiratory infections, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis; situs inversus marks the classic Kartagener subtype.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Laminin in the lamina lucida anchors hemidesmosomes; it has no role in ciliary beating.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lamina densa (type IV collagen) is part of the basal lamina; its loss is not the defect behind recurrent infections with situs inversus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Villin cross-links the actin core of microvilli, which serve absorption and secretion, not airway clearance or organ laterality.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A change to stratified squamous lining is not the lesion of this inherited syndrome; the biopsy in primary ciliary dyskinesia shows ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium with defective axonemes.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A pathology student examining a section of normal skin notes that blood vessels are present only in the connective tissue beneath the epithelium, and none are seen among the epithelial cells themselves. Which of the following best describes how these epithelial cells obtain oxygen and nutrients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arterioles that terminate within the lamina lucida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Capillaries running between the lateral membranes of the cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diffusion from dermal vessels across the basement membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Small vessels penetrating the lamina densa into the epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uptake from the skin surface through apical microvilli

explanation.summary: Epithelium is avascular; its oxygen and nutrients diffuse from vessels in the underlying connective tissue across the basement membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epithelial tissues contain no blood vessels. Vessels in the underlying connective tissue (the dermis in skin, the lamina propria in most internal organs) supply oxygen, nutrients, and signaling molecules, which passively diffuse through the connective tissue and across the basement membrane to the epithelial cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lamina lucida is part of the basal lamina and contains laminins, not terminating arterioles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No capillaries lie between epithelial cells; epithelium is avascular.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vessels do not penetrate the basal lamina into the epithelium; molecules diffuse across it instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epithelial nutrition comes from underlying vessels, not from the external surface.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: An investigator applies a fluorescent antibody against type IV collagen to a section of intestinal mucosa. The label will be concentrated in which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apical brush border

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lamina densa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lamina lucida

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reticular lamina

choices.label: E
choices.text: Terminal bar

explanation.summary: Type IV collagen is a component of the lamina densa of the basal lamina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The basal lamina has two zones. The lamina densa sits beneath the lamina lucida and contains type IV collagen plus various glycoproteins and proteoglycans, forming a network within the basement membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brush border is formed by microvilli with actin cores cross-linked by villin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lamina lucida, next to the plasma membrane, is characterized by laminins that bind hemidesmosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The reticular lamina lies beneath the basal lamina and is derived from connective tissue; reticular fibers are type III collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The terminal bar is a complex of tight and adherent junctions near the apical surface.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: Electron microscopy of a skin biopsy from a 25-year-old woman shows hemidesmosomes along the basal plasma membrane of the deepest epithelial cells. These structures attach the cells to the underlying basal lamina by binding which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Laminin in the lamina lucida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Laminin in the reticular lamina

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type III collagen in the reticular lamina

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type IV collagen in the lamina densa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Villin in the lamina lucida

explanation.summary: Hemidesmosomes bind laminins of the lamina lucida, the basal lamina zone directly against the epithelial cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lamina lucida lies right next to the epithelial cell's plasma membrane and contains laminins, glycoproteins that bind hemidesmosomes, the bridging structures linking the basal lamina to the epithelial cell. Laminins also maintain structural architecture and take part in development, wound healing, and cancer cell invasion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Laminins are located in the lamina lucida, not the connective-tissue-derived reticular lamina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The reticular lamina lies beneath the basal lamina and is derived from connective tissue; hemidesmosomes do not bind it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type IV collagen is in the lamina densa, deeper than the zone that hemidesmosomes bind.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Villin cross-links actin in microvilli; it is not a basal lamina component.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A tracheal biopsy shows tall cells with apical cilia. The nuclei sit at several different heights, giving a layered look, but careful examination shows that every cell rests on the basal lamina. Which of the following best classifies this epithelium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pseudostratified columnar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simple columnar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stratified columnar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stratified cuboidal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transitional

explanation.summary: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is a single layer of columnar cells, all on the basal lamina, whose staggered nuclei falsely suggest stratification.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudostratified epithelium is one layer of columnar cells that all rest on the basal lamina; because the nuclei do not line up, it falsely appears to have multiple layers. It is the respiratory epithelium of the trachea, bronchi, and nasal cavity, and bears cilia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Simple columnar epithelium has nuclei lined up in a uniform row, without the false layered appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stratified columnar epithelium has truly multiple layers, with not every cell reaching the basal lamina; it lines large salivary excretory ducts and parts of the male urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stratified cuboidal epithelium has cube-shaped surface cells and lines sweat gland ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transitional epithelium is truly multilayered and lines the urinary tract, not the trachea.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: Two samples of bladder wall are fixed for histology, one while the bladder was filled to full distension and one while it was empty. Comparing the most superficial epithelial cells in the two samples, which of the following is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciliated when empty, nonciliated when distended

choices.label: B
choices.text: Columnar when distended, flattened when empty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cuboidal in both, since cell shape is fixed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flattened in both, with only basal cells changing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Flattened when distended, cuboidal when empty

explanation.summary: Superficial cells of transitional epithelium look cuboidal in an empty bladder and squamous when the bladder is stretched.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) is a stratified epithelium in tissues that must stretch. Its basal cells are cuboidal or columnar, while its superficial cells change appearance with stretch: cuboidal without stretch (empty bladder) and squamous (flattened) during stretch (full bladder).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Urothelium is not a ciliated epithelium; distension alters cell shape, not surface projections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the pattern; stretch flattens the surface cells rather than making them columnar.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The superficial cells do change shape with distension; that is the hallmark of transitional epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The shape change occurs in the superficial cells; the empty bladder shows cuboidal surface cells.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man who worked for 30 years in an industrial chemical plant is found to have a malignant bladder mass. The tumor most likely arose from which of the following epithelia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pseudostratified columnar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simple columnar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Simple cuboidal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stratified squamous

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transitional

explanation.summary: Bladder transitional epithelium, in steady contact with urine that can carry ingested toxins like industrial chemicals, gives rise to urothelial carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bladder is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium), which is notorious for transforming into urothelial carcinoma (formerly transitional cell carcinoma). Because it is in constant contact with urine, which can contain toxins such as industrial chemicals, it can undergo malignant transformation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is respiratory epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Simple columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestines.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Simple cuboidal epithelium lines renal tubules and the ovary surface, not the bladder.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stratified squamous epithelium lines the vagina, esophagus, and mouth, not the bladder.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: Electron microscopy of a small-intestinal absorptive cell shows short, densely packed apical projections that together give a brush-like appearance. The core of each projection is made of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 9 + 2 microtubule axoneme moved by dynein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Actin filaments cross-linked by villin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Laminin glycoproteins anchored to hemidesmosomes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tight and adherent junction complexes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type IV collagen with associated proteoglycans

explanation.summary: Microvilli have a core of actin filaments cross-linked by villin; packed together they form the brush border.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microvilli are tightly spaced finger-like extensions that increase surface area for absorption and secretion. Their core is actin filaments cross-linked by villin. Because they are short and numerous, intestinal cells bearing them are said to have a brush border.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The 9 + 2 axoneme driven by dynein is the internal structure of motile cilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laminins lie in the lamina lucida at the base of the cell, not in apical projections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tight and adherent junction complexes form the terminal bar between cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type IV collagen and proteoglycans make up the lamina densa of the basal lamina.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A section of the male reproductive tract shows epithelial cells bearing unusually long apical projections. On electron microscopy, these projections contain actin filaments and no axoneme. Which of the following best describes the nature and role of these projections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anchoring fibers that bind the lamina lucida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Junctional complexes that seal adjacent cell borders

choices.label: C
choices.text: Long modified microvilli specialized for absorption

choices.label: D
choices.text: Motile projections that sweep mucus and particulates

choices.label: E
choices.text: True cilia that propel fluid and sperm by beating

explanation.summary: Stereocilia are not true cilia but unusually long microvilli specialized for absorption, found in the male reproductive tract and the inner ear.
explanation.whyCorrect: Despite their name, stereocilia are not cilia; they are unique, long microvilli specialized for absorption. They occur in only a few places, including the male reproductive tract and the sensory components of the inner ear. Lacking an axoneme, they do not beat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemidesmosomes bind laminin in the lamina lucida at the basal, not apical, surface.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Apical junctional complexes (the terminal bar) are tight and adherent junctions, not long surface projections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sweeping of particulates is the role of motile cilia, which need a dynein-driven axoneme.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beating that moves fluid and sperm toward the epididymis is done by true motile cilia of the efferent ductules, which contain 9 + 2 axonemes.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: Renal tubular epithelial cells move ions and molecules from the tubular lumen through the cell to the interstitium, where vessels absorb them. Which property of these epithelial cells makes this one-way transport possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of blood vessels within the epithelial layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Different transporters on the apical and basolateral sides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Identical channels spread evenly over all membrane faces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lack of a basement membrane beneath the tubule cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Villin-linked microvilli covering every membrane surface

explanation.summary: Epithelial polarity, with distinct transporters on apical and basolateral membranes, allows directional transport across renal tubular cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epithelial cells are polarized: the apical membrane (facing away from the basement membrane) and the basolateral membrane carry different receptors, channels, and transporters. In the renal tubule this lets the cell take molecules up from the lumen and release them on the opposite side, after which they pass through the basement membrane into the interstitium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epithelium is avascular, but that explains its nutrient supply, not the direction of transport.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Identical channels everywhere would be the opposite of polarity and would not support one-way transport.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Renal tubules do have a basement membrane surrounding them; transported molecules cross it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microvilli are apical specializations that enlarge surface area; they are not on every surface and do not confer directionality.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman undergoes upper endoscopy for reflux symptoms, and a biopsy is taken from normal-appearing mucosa of the mid-esophagus. Which epithelium is expected in this specimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pseudostratified columnar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simple columnar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stratified columnar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stratified squamous

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transitional

explanation.summary: The esophagus is lined by stratified squamous epithelium, as are the mouth, vagina, and true vocal cords.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stratified squamous epithelium has more than one layer with flat surface cells and is tough and resistant to trauma. It lines the vagina, esophagus, mouth, and true vocal cords.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium lines the trachea, bronchi, and nasal cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Simple columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestines, not the normal esophagus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stratified columnar epithelium lines large salivary excretory ducts and parts of the male urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transitional epithelium lines the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and part of the urethra.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A biopsy taken where the rectum meets the anus shows simple columnar epithelium abruptly changing to stratified squamous epithelium. Which of the following best explains why the two sides differ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both sides absorb water, but the squamous side has more microvilli

choices.label: B
choices.text: The columnar side is ciliated to move stool; the squamous side absorbs ions

choices.label: C
choices.text: The columnar side resists abrasion; the squamous side absorbs water

choices.label: D
choices.text: The columnar side stretches with filling; the squamous side secretes mucus

choices.label: E
choices.text: The columnar side transports water; the squamous side resists trauma

explanation.summary: At the anorectal junction, absorptive rectal columnar epithelium meets the tough, trauma-resistant stratified squamous lining of the anus, an extension of the skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rectum is still part of the absorptive intestine, so its simple columnar epithelium is important in transporting water. The anus is an extension of the outside skin and is lined by tough stratified squamous epithelium that is more resistant to trauma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stratified squamous anal lining is protective, not an absorptive surface with microvilli.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Rectal columnar epithelium is absorptive, not ciliated; motile cilia line airways, fallopian tubes, and efferent ductules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the functions: the squamous lining provides toughness, and the columnar lining handles water transport.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stretching with filling is the property of transitional epithelium in the urinary tract.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A histology student compares two epithelial glands. Gland X releases its product into the space around its cells, where nearby capillaries take it up for circulation to distant organs. Gland Y delivers its product through a duct onto the luminal surface of the duodenum, and the product cannot be detected in the blood. Which of the following glands belongs to the same category as Gland Y?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exocrine pancreas

choices.label: D
choices.text: Islets of Langerhans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Parathyroid glands

explanation.summary: Exocrine glands secrete through ducts onto epithelial surfaces; endocrine glands release hormones into the blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gland Y secretes onto an epithelial surface (the GI lumen) via a duct, the defining feature of an exocrine gland. The exocrine pancreas secretes digestive enzymes (lipase, trypsinogen, amylase) into the GI tract. Its products are not hormones because they do not circulate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The adrenal cortex is an endocrine gland whose hormones circulate in the bloodstream.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The anterior pituitary is an endocrine gland that secretes hormones into the circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The islets are the endocrine part of the pancreas; they release hormones into the blood, like Gland X.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The parathyroid glands are endocrine; their hormones are carried by the blood to target organs.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (2 of 2)

questions.stem: An H&E section of a salivary gland shows a cluster of secretory cells with round, basally located nuclei. The basal cytoplasm of these cells stains an intense purple-blue, while the apical cytoplasm contains small pink granules. The purple-blue staining of the basal cytoplasm is best explained by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant lipid droplets dissolved out during processing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dense bundles of cytokeratin filaments binding the dye

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mucin glycoprotein in the cytoplasm retaining hematoxylin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ribosomal RNA on abundant rough ER binding hematoxylin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stored enzyme granules in the cytoplasm binding eosin

explanation.summary: Serous cell basophilia comes from rRNA on abundant RER binding the basic dye hematoxylin.
explanation.whyCorrect: These are serous cells. Their cytoplasm is basophilic because they are packed with rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes. Ribosomes contain large amounts of negatively charged rRNA, which binds the basic dye hematoxylin; the pink apical granules store proteins and enzymes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Washed-out contents produce pale or clear cytoplasm, not intense basophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytokeratins are intermediate filaments anchoring spot desmosomes; they are not the source of serous basophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucin does not retain most common stains, so mucous cells look clear, not purple-blue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Eosin stains the apical secretory granules pink; it does not produce purple-blue staining.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A biopsy of the uterine cervix shows glandular epithelium in which the secretory cells have pale, almost empty-appearing cytoplasm, with flattened nuclei pressed toward the outer edge of each cell. Which of the following best describes the main product of these cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hormone taken up by nearby capillaries for circulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lipid-rich secretion released as whole cells break apart

choices.label: C
choices.text: A protein-rich fluid released with part of the apical cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: A viscous glycoprotein secretion that lubricates surfaces

choices.label: E
choices.text: A watery protein-rich fluid containing digestive enzymes

explanation.summary: Mucous cells appear clear with flattened peripheral nuclei because mucin does not retain common stains.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucous cells secrete mucus containing the glycoprotein mucin, which is excellent at lubricating surfaces. Mucin does not retain commonly used stains, so the cytoplasm appears clear, with nuclei flattened toward the outer edge. The cervix is one of the listed sites of mucous glands.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hormones are products of endocrine glands; these are surface-secreting exocrine cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That describes holocrine sebum from sebaceous glands of the skin, not cervical glands.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That describes apocrine secretion (mammary, axillary sweat glands), not the clear cells described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: That is a serous secretion; serous cells have basophilic cytoplasm and round central-to-basal nuclei.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A researcher is studying exocrine glands whose secretory cells must die in order to release their product, with the entire cell becoming part of the secretion. Blocking this mode of secretion would most directly reduce the production of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Axillary apocrine sweat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breast milk

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pancreatic digestive enzymes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Saliva

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sebum

explanation.summary: Holocrine secretion (whole cell becomes the secretion) is the mode used by sebaceous glands.
explanation.whyCorrect: In holocrine ('whole-ocrine') secretion, cells accumulate their secretion and then die, becoming part of the product. Sebaceous glands in the skin, which produce sebum, are the lecture's example of holocrine glands.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Armpit sweat glands are apocrine; the cell survives after losing part of its apical cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mammary glands are apocrine: they release product with only a portion of the apical cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The exocrine pancreas is a serous gland; its cells release enzymes without dying.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salivary glands are eccrine (merocrine), releasing product solely by exocytosis.

questions.topicName: Histology of Epithelial Tissue (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 29-year-old lactating woman has a breast biopsy for a palpable lump, which proves benign. The pathologist notes secretory cells in which the apical portion of the cytoplasm is pinched off and released together with the secretory product. Which of the following glands uses the same mode of secretion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Goblet cells of the colon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Parotid salivary gland

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sebaceous glands of the skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sweat glands of the armpit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sweat glands of the forearm

explanation.summary: Apocrine glands (mammary glands, axillary sweat glands) release product with a portion of apical cytoplasm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Losing a portion of the apical cytoplasm with the product defines apocrine secretion ('APical', 'A POrtion'). The lecture's examples are the mammary glands and the apocrine sweat glands in the armpit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Goblet cells are unicellular glands that release mucus by exocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Salivary glands are eccrine (merocrine), secreting solely by exocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sebaceous glands are holocrine: the whole cell dies and becomes the secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: General body-skin sweat glands are eccrine glands used for body cooling.

questions.stem: The epithelium lining the GI tract must resist the shearing forces generated as food moves along it. A junction that encircles each cell like a band near its apex and connects neighboring cells helps resist these forces. On the cytoplasmic side, this junction is linked to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actin filaments by way of catenins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Actin filaments by way of zonula occludens proteins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cytokeratin filaments by way of plaques

choices.label: D
choices.text: Laminin of the lamina lucida by way of integrins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neighboring cytoplasm by way of connexons

explanation.summary: Belt desmosomes (zonulae adherens) use cadherins bound to catenins that link to actin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The belt desmosome (zonula adherens, adherens junction) wraps around the cell and helps resist shearing forces, such as in the GI tract. Its bridges are cadherins, whose cytoplasmic ends bind catenins that link to actin filaments through actin-binding proteins.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ZO proteins anchor tight junction claudins and occludins to actin, not the cadherins of the belt.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anchorage to intermediate filaments (cytokeratins) is characteristic of spot desmosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Integrin-laminin linkage describes hemidesmosomes, which anchor cells to the basement membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Connexons are the channels of gap junctions, which mediate communication.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph of stratified epithelium shows small, disk-shaped dense plaques on the lateral membranes of adjacent cells, into which bundles of cytokeratin filaments insert on each side. The intercellular bridges at these plaques are formed by which of the following proteins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Catenins bound to actin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claudins and occludins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connexins assembled into connexons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desmoglein and desmocollin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Integrins bound to laminin

explanation.summary: Spot desmosomes are bridged by the cadherins desmoglein and desmocollin and anchor cytokeratin filaments.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disk-shaped adhesive plaques anchored to intermediate filaments (cytokeratins) are spot desmosomes (maculae adherens). Like belt desmosomes, their bridges are cadherin-family proteins, specifically desmoglein and desmocollin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Catenins are intracellular linkers of belt desmosomes; they are not the bridging proteins here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Claudins and occludins are the transmembrane proteins of tight junctions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Connexins build the channels of gap junctions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Integrins bind laminin at hemidesmosomes, attaching cells to the basement membrane.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man develops widespread blisters of the skin. Serum testing identifies autoantibodies against desmoglein. The function of which of the following structures is most directly disrupted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Belt desmosomes (zonulae adherens)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gap junctions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemidesmosomes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spot desmosomes (maculae adherens)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tight junctions (zonulae occludens)

explanation.summary: Pemphigus vulgaris: antibodies to desmoglein disrupt spot desmosomes, causing blistering.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is pemphigus vulgaris, a rare blistering disease of middle-aged and older adults. Antibodies against desmoglein, a bridging protein of spot desmosomes, disrupt the linkage between epithelial cells in the skin and cause blisters.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Belt desmosomes use cadherins such as E-cadherin, not desmoglein.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gap junctions are built from connexins and mediate communication, not adhesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemidesmosomes are targeted in bullous pemphigoid and attach cells to the basal lamina via integrins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tight junctions are built from claudins and occludins.

questions.stem: A 76-year-old woman has tense blisters in the groin and axillae and erosions in her mouth. Immunofluorescence of a lesional biopsy shows antibodies deposited along the dermal-epidermal junction. The autoantibodies most likely impair a structure that is characterized by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Belt desmosome bridged by E-cadherin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gap junction formed by connexins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemidesmosome attached by integrins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spot desmosome bridged by desmoglein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tight junction sealed by claudins

explanation.summary: Bullous pemphigoid: autoantibodies against a hemidesmosome component detach epithelium from the basal lamina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bullous pemphigoid is caused by autoantibodies binding a component of the hemidesmosomes, so epithelial cells no longer attach well to the basal lamina, producing blisters in the groin, axilla, and oral cavity. Immunofluorescence shows antibodies at the dermal-epidermal junction. Hemidesmosomes attach cells to the basement membrane through integrins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Belt desmosomes join neighboring epithelial cells; E-cadherin loss is linked to tumor invasion, not this blistering pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gap junctions mediate cell-to-cell communication, not attachment to the basement membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-desmoglein disease (pemphigus vulgaris) targets cell-to-cell spot desmosomes, not attachment at the dermal-epidermal junction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tight junctions seal the intercellular space and maintain polarity; they do not anchor cells to the basal lamina.

questions.stem: Each heartbeat depends on the rapid transfer of ions from one cardiac muscle cell to the next so that contraction is coordinated. The channels that permit this direct cell-to-cell ion transfer are formed by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cadherins linked to catenins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claudins and occludins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connexins forming connexons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desmoglein and desmocollin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Integrins bound to laminin

explanation.summary: Gap junctions, made of connexins forming connexons, allow direct ion transfer between cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gap junctions contain connexins that form a cylindrical connexon, a tube allowing direct transfer of small ions and molecules between cells. In cardiac muscle they permit the rapid ion transfer needed to coordinate each heartbeat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cadherin-catenin complexes form adhesive belt desmosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These seal tight junctions and limit passage between cells rather than connecting cytoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These bridge spot desmosomes for adhesion, not communication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Integrins attach hemidesmosomes to the basement membrane.

questions.stem: In renal tubular epithelium, sodium is absorbed into each cell by transport proteins on one surface and pumped out by different transport proteins on the opposite surface. A mutation in which of the following would most directly allow solutes to bypass this route by moving passively between adjacent cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cadherins and catenins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claudins and occludins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Connexins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desmoglein and desmocollin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Integrins

explanation.summary: Tight junctions (claudins, occludins) prevent passive leakage of molecules between epithelial cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transcellular transport only works if molecules cannot leak passively between cells. Tight junctions (zonula occludens) seal neighboring membranes to prevent this; they are made of the transmembrane proteins claudins and occludins, anchored to actin by zonula occludens proteins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These form belt desmosomes that bind cells together and resist shear, not seal the paracellular space.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Connexins form gap junction channels that connect the cytoplasms of neighboring cells; they do not seal the intercellular space.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These bridge spot desmosomes, providing strength rather than sealing the space between cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Integrins attach hemidesmosomes to laminin of the basement membrane.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man has a firm nodule on his neck that has been incised and drained twice, yet it refilled with greasy material each time. Pathology after excision shows a cyst lined by epithelium associated with a sebaceous gland. Which of the following best explains both how the cyst contents are produced and why the lesion recurred?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apical cytoplasm pinches off into the secretion; incomplete drainage left sebum behind

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apical cytoplasm pinches off into the secretion; the cyst wall was left in place

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vesicles fuse with the apical membrane; the cyst wall was left in place

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whole cells disintegrate into the secretion; incomplete drainage left sebum behind

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whole cells disintegrate into the secretion; the cyst wall was left in place

explanation.summary: Sebaceous glands are holocrine; a sebaceous cyst recurs unless its epithelial wall and gland are excised.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sebaceous glands accumulate lipid-rich secretion until the entire cell breaks apart and becomes part of the sebum (holocrine). Drainage removes only the accumulated material and leaves the epithelial lining and glandular structures, so the cyst reforms; complete excision of the cyst wall greatly reduces recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both parts are wrong: sebaceous glands are holocrine, and recurrence reflects the retained lining.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Releasing a portion of apical cytoplasm is apocrine secretion, not the holocrine mode of sebaceous glands.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Release purely by exocytosis is eccrine (merocrine) secretion, not sebaceous secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mode is correct, but residual contents do not explain recurrence; the retained epithelial lining does.
